title: Worked examples
instruction: Select the heading to open the worked example.

_items.title: Worked example
_items.body:
Consider two sport and exercise science students revising the same difficult theory for an exam.

Tomos asks a chatbot to explain the theory and summarise the key points, then rereads the summary until it feels familiar. It all makes sense on the screen. In the exam, asked to apply the theory to a new case, Tomos cannot do it. The tool had done the thinking, and the understanding was never built.

Cerys uses the same chatbot to explain the theory, then closes it and writes the explanation out from memory in their own words. Cerys asks the tool what the explanation missed, fixes the gaps, and works through a practice case. The tool helped Cerys learn without learning in Cerys's place.

Both used AI to revise. Only Cerys stayed the one doing the thinking, and so could use the theory when it counted.

_items.title: Worked example
_items.body:
Consider two sport and exercise science students who ask a chatbot to summarise the evidence on a contested question for a sport science essay.

Elen gets a fluent summary with a striking statistic and three named studies. It reads as though an expert wrote it, so Elen builds the essay around the figure and cites the studies. The statistic was invented, one study does not exist, and only one side of the debate appears. Nothing was checked, and the essay rests on things that were never true.

Ynyr gets a similar summary and treats it as a set of leads, not facts. Ynyr tries to verify the statistic and cannot find it, checks each study in the library, and notices a major counter-argument is missing. Ynyr keeps what holds up, drops the rest, and reads more widely to fill the gap.

Both got the same confident answer. Only Ynyr read it critically, and so caught the invented figure, the false source and the missing side.

_items.title: Hallucination
_items.body: The tool states things that are simply made up: invented facts, events, authors or citations, presented as real. It is the most common and most damaging failure, because the fabrication looks exactly like genuine content.
